solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Actress to cut back completely, seeing weight on these?

parts.note: to prune is to cut or trim

indicators.note: back says the word for completely is read the other way round

parts.note: all means completely, as in 'all wrong'
scales are the device you read a weight on

explanation.surface: A cryptic nudge about an actress who might be weighed after trimming herself down completely.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns ALL into LLA. Prunella Scales is an English actress, best known as Sybil in the sitcom Fawlty Towers.
explanation.definitionFit: The full name belongs to a well-known English stage and television performer.

clue.text: Approach stern of catamaran found in wreck

indicators.note: found in says one piece sits inside another

parts.note: to wreck is to ruin

indicators.note: the stern is the back of a boat, so the last letter of the word catamaran

explanation.surface: A sailor comes in to land and finds the back of the boat smashed up.
explanation.definitionFit: A run-up or lead-in period is the approach to an event, as in the run-up to a race.

clue.text: Lifted underwear to stop itch — it's within reach

indicators.note: in a down clue, lifted means the whole build is read from the bottom up
to stop is to plug, sitting inside the word for itch

parts.note: a yen is an itch or longing
a bra is an item of underwear

explanation.surface: Hoisting up your bra to relieve an itch, which is handily close by.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down light 'Lifted' reads the whole assembly from bottom to top, so YBRAEN becomes the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Something close at hand is in easy reach; the definition is a phrase describing the adjective.

clue.text: One might do this with a fast crew, down around banks of Seine earlier

definitions.text: One might do this with a fast

indicators.note: earlier says this part comes before the word for crew
around says the word for down encloses the banks

parts.note: feeling down is feeling low

indicators.note: the banks of a river are its two edges, here the outside letters of the word Seine

parts.note: an eight is a rowing crew, as in the Boat Race

explanation.surface: A rowing crew heading down the Seine, past its banks.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface pictures a fast boat crew, but 'a fast' is a period without food. 'earlier' puts LOSEW in front of EIGHT.
explanation.definitionFit: Fasting, going without food, is a common way of trying to slim down.

clue.text: Wolfgang's agreed to hoist American guitar hero

indicators.note: in a down clue, hoisting means the word is read upwards, that is backwards

parts.note: Wolfgang suggests a German, and ja is German for yes
ax is the American spelling of axe, slang for a guitar

explanation.surface: A German musician agrees to lift up a guitar for an American rock star.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a guitar hero, but the hero is the Greek warrior Ajax of the Trojan War.
explanation.definitionFit: Ajax is a warrior of Greek legend who fought at Troy, a hero of Homer's Iliad.

clue.text: Exclusive alcoholic drink men discarded in church yard

indicators.note: in says the trimmed drink sits inside the church

parts.note: CE is the Church of England

indicators.note: discarded says the word for men is dropped from the drink

parts.note: liquor is strong alcoholic drink
OR, other ranks, are soldiers who are not officers, so men

explanation.surface: A private drinks party in a churchyard, with the men thrown out.
explanation.walkthrough: OR, 'other ranks', is the army's term for enlisted soldiers as opposed to officers, so crosswords use it for men.
explanation.definitionFit: A cliquey group is a closed circle that keeps outsiders away, so it is exclusive.

clue.text: Being green, Elsa's recycled bottles very well

indicators.note: to bottle is to hold something within, so the rearranged letters enclose the other piece
recycled means the letters are reprocessed into a new order

parts.note: fine can mean very well, as in feeling fine

explanation.surface: An environmentally minded Elsa takes her bottles to be recycled, which is very good of her.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recycled' gives LEASS. The recycling surface makes 'green' look environmental, but it means leafy greenery.
explanation.definitionFit: Leafiness is the state of having a lot of foliage, and so of being green.

clue.text: Rung female supremo to get hold of fruit scientist

parts.note: a step is a rung of a ladder

indicators.note: to get hold of something is to grip it, so the fruit goes inside

parts.note: a hen is a female bird
a king is a supreme ruler
a haw is the fruit of the hawthorn

explanation.surface: Someone telephoned a female boss to get some fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rung' looks like a verb (phoned) but is the noun, a step on a ladder.
explanation.definitionFit: The British physicist known for his work on black holes and A Brief History of Time.

clue.text: Writer's deviously aiming to obtain riches with document

parts.note: a will is a legal document

indicators.note: to obtain is to take in, so the rearranged letters hold the word for riches
deviously says the letters go round about, out of order

parts.note: gold stands for riches

explanation.surface: A writer schemes to get a fortune by means of a document, a forged will perhaps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'deviously' gives IAMING, which 'to obtain' opens after its fourth letter. The 's of 'Writer's' is a link meaning 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: The English novelist who wrote Lord of the Flies and won the Nobel Prize for literature.

clue.text: Scottish island engages native perhaps draining sewage in mass of water

indicators.note: to engage is to take on or hold, so the island holds the rest

parts.note: Iona is a Scottish island off Mull
Ian is a typical Scottish first name, so a native of Scotland, perhaps

indicators.note: draining empties the word sewage of its inside, leaving its outer letters

explanation.surface: A Scottish island takes on a local to drain its sewage into the sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'draining' empties 'sewage' of its middle, and 'engages' opens the island just before its final A. Ian is a stock Scottish first name, hence a 'native perhaps'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Ionian Sea is the arm of the Mediterranean between Italy and Greece, a large body of water.

clue.text: Foolish characters adversely involved in shenanigans

indicators.note: adversely means going against, so the letters run in the opposite direction
involved in says the letters are contained within the next word

explanation.surface: Silly characters are mixed up in some mischief.
explanation.walkthrough: 'involved in' finds ENANI within 'shenanigans', and 'adversely' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: Inane means silly or senseless, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: After extensive help in fiddling, one's fired

indicators.note: after says the word for help in fiddling follows the word for extensive

parts.note: long means extensive in length
a bow is what a fiddler draws across the strings

explanation.surface: After a lot of help with some fraud, someone loses their job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fiddling' suggests cheating and 'fired' a sacking, but the fiddling is violin playing and the firing is shooting arrows.
explanation.definitionFit: A tall bow used by medieval English archers, so a weapon that is shot or discharged.

clue.text: Correct sort of wordplay?

definitions.meaning: to correct here is to discipline someone for wrongdoing
read as PUN plus ISH, the word suggests something rather like a pun; the question mark admits this is fanciful

explanation.surface: A short question about putting wordplay right.
explanation.definitionFit: To discipline or chastise someone is to make them pay for wrongdoing; the second reading is a playful split.

clue.text: 'Covert' might be thus in dictionary

parts.note: in a dictionary the word covert comes just after the entry cover, so it is found beneath that headword

explanation.surface: Where you might find the word for secret when looking it up.
explanation.walkthrough: Split as two words the answer says where the entry sits; as one word it means secret, which is what covert means.
explanation.definitionFit: Secret or concealed, a synonym of covert, while the split phrase gives its place in a word list.

clue.text: Having arrived, first couple swapped top

indicators.note: the first two letters of the word for having arrived change places

parts.note: came means having arrived, as in 'came home'

explanation.surface: When they arrived, the leading pair exchanged a top, a garment perhaps.
explanation.definitionFit: The acme is the peak or highest point of something.

clue.text: Chairman hosts themed event after backing in party programme

indicators.note: a host holds guests, so the chairman's name contains the rest

parts.note: Chairman Mao, the Chinese communist leader

indicators.note: after says the event comes behind the turned-round word
backing means going backwards, so the word in is read the other way round

parts.note: a fest is a festival or gathering with a theme, as in beer fest

explanation.surface: A chairman hosts a themed party after getting support.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' looks like support, but it turns 'in' round; 'after' and 'hosts' then build NIFEST inside the chairman's name.
explanation.definitionFit: A manifesto is a political party's published statement of policies, the programme it campaigns on.

clue.text: Organ reaches peak maintaining a pulse

parts.note: a kidney is a bodily organ

indicators.note: to maintain is to hold or keep, so the word for peak holds the letter a

parts.note: a ben is a Scottish mountain peak, as in Ben Nevis

explanation.surface: A medical picture: an organ reaches its peak while the heart keeps a steady pulse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pulse' looks like a heartbeat but here it is an edible seed of a pod plant. 'reaches' simply joins the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Pulses are edible seeds such as beans, lentils and peas; a kidney bean is one such legume.

clue.text: Female entered urging the new protagonist in Western?

indicators.note: entered says one piece goes in among the other letters
new means the letters are made afresh in a different order

explanation.surface: A woman walked in, pushing the latest hero of a cowboy film.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' rearranges URGINGTHE into GUNIGHTER, and 'entered' puts F inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Westerns typically centre on a gunslinger hero; the question mark marks this as an example only.

clue.text: Main danger one hundred endure around work unit

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
C is the Roman numeral for a hundred

indicators.note: around here means turned about, so the verb is reversed

parts.note: to be is to exist or endure
the erg is a unit of work in physics

explanation.surface: The chief danger to a unit at work is one hundred people having to put up with it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Main' is the sea, as in poetry, not 'chief'. 'around' turns the verb round rather than enclosing anything.
explanation.definitionFit: Floating ice is a hazard to shipping on the open sea, the main in old poetic English.

clue.text: Bones in duck and turkey withdrawn

parts.note: a duck is a score of nought in cricket, so O

indicators.note: withdrawn means pulled back, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: a turkey is a fool or failure, and so is an ass

explanation.surface: Bones are found in a duck and a turkey, removed from the carcass.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turkey' means a fool here, not the bird.
explanation.definitionFit: Ossa is the Latin plural of os, the anatomical word for bone.

clue.text: In which tea is the language of love?

definitions.text: In which tea is the language of love?

parts.words: In which tea is the language of love?
parts.note: the tongue thought of as romantic, where the word for tea is thé, spelt like English 'the'

explanation.surface: A riddle about tea and romance.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'tea is the' literally: in this language the word for tea is the, with an accent the clue leaves off.
explanation.definitionFit: The tongue of France is popularly thought of as the most romantic one.

clue.text: Had a fling frequently — in the French department initially

indicators.note: in says the word for frequently goes inside the French article

parts.note: le is French for the
oft is an old word for often

indicators.note: initially means only the first letter of the word department is used

explanation.surface: Someone had many affairs while working in the French department.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Had a fling' suggests a romance, but here it means threw, as in flinging a ball high.
explanation.definitionFit: To loft something is to throw or hit it high into the air, so to fling it.

clue.text: Nag artist that's rejected one thousand dollars? It may be a lot in US

definitions.text: It may be a lot in US

parts.note: to carp is to nag or complain

indicators.note: rejected means thrown back, so the artist's letters are reversed

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, an artist
K stands for a thousand, so a grand

explanation.surface: Nagging an artist who turned down a thousand dollars, which might be a lot of money in America.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a lot' suggests a large sum but means a parking lot, the American term for a car park.
explanation.definitionFit: Americans call an area for leaving vehicles a parking lot, so this is one.

clue.text: Excuse old politician receiving fine? On the contrary

indicators.note: receiving says one piece takes in another
on the contrary reverses the receiving, so the word for fine holds the politician

parts.note: A1 means first-rate or fine, written here as AI
a Lib is a member of the old Liberal Party, before it merged into the Lib Dems

explanation.surface: An old politician makes excuses when receiving a fine, or the other way round.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On the contrary' flips 'receiving', so A1 (written AI) holds LIB rather than LIB holding it.
explanation.definitionFit: An alibi is a claim of being elsewhere, an excuse offered for wrongdoing.

clue.text: Having a nap, losing party spirit

indicators.note: losing means the party's letters are dropped

parts.note: dozing is having a nap
a do is a party

explanation.surface: Someone nodding off at a party is losing their spirit.
explanation.definitionFit: Zing is liveliness or energy, a synonym of spirit in the sense of vigour.

clue.text: Some homeless people deal with such when facing big kids

definitions.text: Some homeless people deal with such when facing big
definitions.meaning: A British magazine sold on the street by homeless people, so it is what follows 'big'

explanation.surface: Homeless people dealing with big kids.
explanation.walkthrough: The Big Issue is a UK street magazine sold by homeless vendors. The clue reads as if 'big kids' go together, but 'big' belongs to the first definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Offspring, children, are a legal term for descendants; the other sense completes a magazine name.

clue.text: Independent group of delegates ignoring fellow's deceit

indicators.note: ignoring means leaving out the part for fellow

parts.note: a convention is a gathering of delegates
co- is a prefix meaning fellow or joint, as in co-pilot

explanation.surface: An independent delegate accuses the conference of trickery once a colleague is ignored.
explanation.definitionFit: An invention can be a made-up story, a fabrication or falsehood, and so a deceit.

clue.text: Composer steadily grew on Reg, twice playing disc taken from show at home

indicators.note: steadily suggests a regular step, taking every other letter of grew on
playing means the letters are messing about in a new order
twice means the name is used two times over

parts.note: Reg is taken as written

indicators.note: taken from means the disc is removed from the word show

parts.note: a disc is round, like the letter O
in means at home, as in 'staying in'

explanation.surface: A musical picture: Reg steadily grows on you, playing a disc taken from a show at home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'steadily' takes GEO from 'grew on'; 'twice' and 'playing' rearrange REGREG into RGEGER; 'taken from' drops O from SHOW, leaving SHW.
explanation.definitionFit: The American composer of Rhapsody in Blue and Porgy and Bess.
